messages:
maya: quick update — ran a short 'pulse' sampling pass on a prod-like replica to capture kernel hotspots with minimal overhead. 30s window, 1% sampling, and a tiny nsys timeline crop. attaching the gist and a short summary.

maya: why: full nsys traces kill tails and change scheduling. pulse sampling tries to get a representative kernel mix (conv, matmul, softmax, kv-cache) while keeping p99 impact <1%.

maya: command used:```bash
nsys profile -t cuda,cudnn,osrt -w true -s sampling -f true -o /tmp/pulse_1987654321 
  --sampling-frequency=100 --duration=30 --target-processes=pid:$(pgrep runtime)
```

maya: quick numbers from the run: total samples=~3.2k, kernel samples=~2.8k, estimated added latency on avg requests ~0.4ms, observed 99th delta during window +1.2ms (saw 2 spikes coincident with long KV miss eviction).

sam: nice. can you paste the top-5 kernel stack names and weights? interested if matmul-epilogue or softmax is the culprit.

maya: top kernels: 
- fused_gemm_dispatch (38%)
- kv_cache_lookup (21%)
- softmax_with_scale (12%)
- layernorm_fwd (9%)
- cudaMemcpyAsync (6%)
(full list in gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/pulse-1987654321) :link:

liam: kv_cache_lookup at 21% is surprising — is that cold-start noise? was the run after a restart or with synthetic traffic?

maya: synthetic traffic with realistic prompt mixes. we intentionally hit some cold prefixes to exercise cache behavior. KV lookup skew increases during lots of short-context queries.

kai: idea: make sampling window align to traffic seasons — e.g., sample 30s every 10min, and only when p50 latency < threshold to avoid conflating throttling. we should also disable sampling during rollouts.

sam: question on sampling bias: 1% sampling at 100Hz — do we undercount short kernels (<200us)? how do we normalize weights?

maya: we normalize by sample count / kernel_duration_estimate to get per-token time share. for very short kernels we use a min-duration floor (50us) to avoid inflating counts. still an approximation but matches our offline perf runs within ~10%.

liam: can we automatically switch to a low-overhead trace (light perfetto timeline) when we detect rising kv_cache miss rate? i.e., adaptive tracing triggered by metric anomaly.

maya: yes. proposal:
- baseline: pulse sampling (30s @1% every 10m)
- anomaly trigger: kv_miss_rate > 0.8% sustained for 30s OR p99 delta > 2ms
- on trigger: spin a 60s perfetto microtrace with fine kernel timestamps (not full nsys) and collect kernel launch timings + GPU-sched markers

kai: guardrails: enforce max extra latency budget per request during sampling window. if measured p99 delta > 3ms for 3 consecutive windows, kill sampling for 30m and create alert.

ops-bot: deploy-bot noticed a canary deploy 1987654300 -> runtime-v1.22.3 during the sampling window (note: sampling was disabled for canary by default).

maya: good catch — that canary overlapped with some runs, but we excluded canary-hosts in analysis. will re-run a clean pulse tomorrow morning.

sam: last thought — we should record the sampling config in trace metadata (freq, window, pid, commit) and correlate with rollout tags. otherwise noisy experiments will pollute long-term tooling.

maya: agreed. adding fields: sampling_mode=pulse, freq=100Hz, pct=1, window_s=30, trigger_policy=kv_miss|latency, git_sha=ab12c3d.

liam: can you drop a short playbook line for oncall? e.g., how to interpret a KV surge vs a kernel perf regression.

maya: summary for oncall (one-liner):
- KV surge: look for increased kv_cache_lookup % + high eviction rate -> usually warmup or input distribution change. workarounds: short-term cache-size bump, routing to dedicated capacity.
- Kernel regression: sudden rise in fused_gemm_dispatch or softmax% across all hosts -> treat as potential kernel binary/regression; roll back recent runtime or kernel lib update, run full nsys offline on a repro node.

kai: adding to runbook under /docs/runbooks/light-sampling-playbook.md :+1:

maya: thanks all — re-run scheduled 06:15 UTC, will post updated timeline and the perfetto microtrace if anomaly fires.

sam: thanks, appreciate the short-window approach. less noisy than full traces.

kai: bringing this to the weekly runtime sync — this adaptive pulse idea feels like a good guardrail set.

ops-bot: alert: sampling disabled automatically for 30m due to p99 delta > 3ms (rule enforcement) — incident ticket #INC-1242 created.

maya: noted. follow-up once the incident is triaged.
